teams.heading: Jake White drafts Nathan Hughes into Fiji's extended squad for November Tests
teams.body: Former England international Nathan Hughes will return to Test rugby in November after being drafted into Jake White's 35-man Fiji squad for the Nations Championship. Hughes won 22 England caps between 2016 and 2019. He is one of four uncapped players in the group, with Peniami Narisia, Marika Parker and Setareki Bituniyata, and Planet Rugby reports White could give all four their first Test caps this month.

lead.why: It is a new national-team selection item for Fiji, and the other recent candidates are already reported or concern other nations.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock given freedom to shine in Northampton's 28-14 win over Gloucester
teams.body: Planet Rugby's takeaways from Saturday's 28-14 win at Franklin's Gardens frame Northampton's handling of Henry Pollock as a deliberate call, taking him out of the firing line so the recalled England powerhouse could shine. The Saints trailed 14-0 early before their forwards battered through the heart of Gloucester to level at the break, with Tom Pearson, back in the England picture this autumn, outstanding throughout, according to the Guardian.

lead.why: It is a new item on England's recalled player Henry Pollock, and it is not the Mitchell injury already reported in today's edition.

teams.heading: France beat Fiji 34-21 at home in their last meeting
teams.body: Fiji's last visit to France came in the International Friendlies in November 2025, and they left on the wrong end of a 34-21 scoreline. In the log, France are 3 of 12, with two wins and one defeat from three matches. Across those three, France have scored 116 points and conceded 75. Their most recent result was a 42-15 win over Japan in Round 3.

teams.heading: Jamie Benson reveals Farrell called him into Ireland training before Ulster move
teams.body: Ulster's Jamie Benson, 24, calls the call-up a shock. Farrell brought him into training in July, before he had set foot in Ulster after leaving Harlequins. “Obviously, it was a bit of a shock to be called in here before I’d even set foot in Ulster, but it was a great feeling,” Benson says. His mother Carole, who grew up in Belfast, was delighted, though she was careful not to push him towards Ireland, and he is now in the Ireland squad.

teams.heading: Italy U18 beat Ireland 36-29 as Agressi try seals comeback
teams.body: Italy's Under 18s beat Ireland 36-29 at Badia Polesine on Saturday, repeating last year's win in Cosenza after trailing 17-12 at the break. The Azzurrini were down to 13 men after Amurri's yellow card and Nikitakos's second yellow, and Ireland stretched the lead to 22-12. Fanzo's try got Italy back into it, and Agressi's try put them 26-22 ahead in the 15th minute of the second half. Captain Mesaglio had opened Italy's scoring.

lead.why: It is the only new Italy-team item in the pack, and no senior national-team news is covered today.

teams.heading: Fergus Watson named Player of the Match as Glasgow beat Lions 28-20
teams.body: Glasgow's 28-20 win over the Lions at Scotstoun on Halloween weekend was a showcase for Scotland's young talent, with Fergus Watson named Player of the Match after opening the scoring off a Dan Lancaster cross kick. Lancaster crossed for the second before half-time, and the Warriors led 19-3 at the break. The Lions rallied through Morne van den Berg and Siba Mahashe, but Ollie Smith's late try was not enough, and George Horne's late penalty denied them a bonus point.

lead.why: The Glasgow result is the freshest pick left on the shortlist that the fan has not already read, and it carries a Scotland prospects angle.

teams.heading: Wales release Josh Adams to play for Cardiff in Welsh derby
teams.body: The 31-year-old has played just twice this season, so Wales let him go back to Cardiff for the Ospreys match to get more game time. Adams was a regular for Wales last year, starting two autumn Tests and every Six Nations game, and returned to action earlier this month. Meanwhile Tom Rogers, Dan Edwards, Reuben Morgan-Williams and Gareth Thomas were in Wales camp preparing for the Japan Test.

lead.why: It is the strongest Wales men's item left after the Adams try and Lynn's women's side story were ruled out, and it names a Wales player and a Wales decision.

teams.heading: Facundo Isa recalled to Argentina squad for Ireland, replacing injured Santiago Grondona
teams.body: Contepomi's first Nations Championship roster, finalised for the Dublin opener, brings back a veteran who had been away from the set-up. Facundo Isa comes in for the injured Santiago Grondona, and the report notes he last played for Argentina in July 2025. The November roster is the first without second-rower Franco Molina, with veteran Tomás Lavanini back instead.

lead.why: A national-team selection change, with a veteran back in the squad, is a fresh item that a fan would talk about and is not covered by the earlier editions.

teams.heading: Leicester Fainga'anuku named in All Blacks' northern squad after missing July games
teams.body: Stephen Donald, the former All Blacks fly-half, says Fainga'anuku's hybrid skill set could change how Rennie builds his bench. The 27-year-old, who has played mostly at centre or wing but started games at openside flanker in Super Rugby Pacific this year, can cover both 5-3 and 6-2 roles. Donald also floated a bench with two loose forwards. He is expected to feature in the matchday 23, with Rennie naming the first northern Test team next week.

lead.why: Fainga'anuku's November squad inclusion is a fresh national-team selection item, and it is not one of the three stories already reported.

teams.heading: Mchunu and Louw named in Erasmus' Nations Championship squad after Stormers win
teams.body: Saturday's 33-7 win over Ulster in Cape Town was built up front, where Ntuthuko Mchunu and Wilco Louw regularly sent the visitors' scrum into reverse. That, plus the Stormers' maul superiority, let the hosts march up the field from their own half. Both Springboks have been named in Rassie Erasmus' Nations Championship squad, and the home side's excellence up front was a significant reason Ulster could not take advantage of the Stormers' handling errors.

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new item: a national-team squad inclusion for two Springboks, which outranks the already-reported Furlong and Hansen stories.
